analysis_status: effect-blind directional replication design frozen before dyad-level gain/loss effects were inspected

source.article: Dominguez-Garcia et al. 2026 Ecology Letters e70293

gain.interpretation: pooled axis difference is essentially zero and does not rescue the primary gain-direction mismatch

loss.interpretation: plant-side loss dominance persists when plant abundance replaces plant phenology

cross_system_read.supported: Within the independent 12-site binary observed-link surface, the Villavicencio plant-side loss direction reappears directionally under the focal-excluded predictor definition.
cross_system_read.not_supported: The Villavicencio pollinator-side gain direction does not reappear, and neither endpoint can be promoted to a detection-defensible latent-state mechanism because the external annual binary response does not pass the response-validity gate.
cross_system_read.revised_hypothesis: Observed-link opportunity structure can show repeatable endpoint asymmetries across systems, but the exact plant/pollinator allocation is context-dependent and latent ecological gain/loss remains unverified without detection-defensible state information.
cross_system_read.importance: The external test is now used as an out-of-site robustness pattern on recorded links, not as ecological-state replication.

not_established: cross-system replication of latent ecological gain/loss mechanisms
causal plant control of link loss
why the gain-side axis differs between systems
dyad-level true absence for unrecorded annual links
equivalence of measurement scales across datasets
claim_ceiling: External predictive-direction result on recorded annual links only. The plant-side loss direction is consistent on the observed-link surface, while the gain-side direction is not; the response-validity gate does not admit either as detection-defensible latent ecological state replication. Do not promote these patterns to causal assembly/disassembly mechanisms or routeability.

response_validity.interpretation: Leave-one-site-out axis directions are predictions of recorded annual link gain/loss. The public processed surface does not identify latent link-state transitions.
